entries.title: Reported ETH refutation by deterministic bounded-width SAT
entries.claim: For each fixed k >= 2, the selected Lean target states exact counting and SAT decision on canonical k-CNF with n variables and L encoding bits in (L+1)^O_k(1) * 2^O_k(n*(log log n)^2/sqrt(log n)) time and polynomial all-prefix visited-tape space. This contradicts ETH and standard fixed-width SETH if established. Anthropic independently gives a uniform counting algorithm. An external verifier reports a successful default-kernel comparison of OpenAI’s pinned solution.
assumptions: Inspected scope, canonical formula/encoding and primitive-machine definitions, comparator configuration and solution theorem reached through the configured Main module; no transitive proof build, comparator replay or measured dependency audit was performed here. The challenge placeholder is separate from the solution proof.

The external log reports the measured dependencies propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The verifier used cached Mathlib and the default Lean kernel. The sharper manuscript bounds are separate from this formal target.

Clause width is fixed; constants and polynomial degrees may depend on k. Polynomial visited-tape space is not a finite target memory budget, and no practical crossover or implementation speedup is established.

The result does not settle P versus NP, independent OV/OMv conjectures, universal proof search or termination, or concrete MLWE/MSIS/hash security. Removing an ETH/SETH premise does not construct faster algorithms for every problem with a conditional lower bound.

consumer.owner: Q5b placement; U-05 schedule producer; Q34f/Q34h workload selection

entries.title: Integer multiplication on tapes and earlier constructions
entries.claim: OpenAI’s November fixed deterministic multitape machine writes the full product of two n-bit integers in n*(log n)^(1/2+o(1)) worst-case steps with O(n) visited cells. Weak ETH gives a lower bound of order n*sqrt(log n) even for the low n bits. The earlier conditional CrocSwap constructions and platypii’s separate end-to-end Lean theorem carry their own evidence.
assumptions: Weak ETH excludes deterministic 3-SAT in 2^O(v^(1-eta))*poly(L) for any fixed 0 < eta < 1. The October subexponential algorithms do not attain this scale. Even under Weak ETH the optimal log exponent is an infimum and exact attainment is open.

The selected record, AI-assisted changed-interface review and supplied 23-stage/59-artifact validation receipt were inspected; their verifiers and complete transitive proof stack were not independently replayed or reviewed here.

For CrocSwap's selected construction, native producer/movement, fixed-tape execution, precision, fine-prime padding, analytic decomposition and exact recovery remain inherited premises; its larger saving has no complete formal or independent human verification here.

Later CrocSwap package statements and intake dispositions were inspected, not independently replayed. Archival merge is not scientific admission; sufficient supplier rank and its exponent reductions are neither a multiplication-input threshold nor a measured speedup.

The separate Lean statement, public proof, final transform-cost discharge, pinned Mathlib computation definition and audit source were inspected. Its one fixed FinTM2 machine computes exact products for every natural-number pair in standard binary; the asymptotic worst-case bound uses total encoded input length. Model correspondence and the full transitive development have not been independently reviewed or rebuilt here.

Lean CI run 39718287684 at 228513faf7ebca347d345c187687a379bfb5ed8c reports successful build, AxiomAudit and CompletedProofCheck steps. Audit source permits propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; CI step metadata and an allowlist are not an independent kernel replay. The source theorem's saving is recorded; README parameter prose is stale.

entries.title: Deterministic linear-time minimum spanning tree
entries.claim: Khanna, Putterman and Song claim deterministic comparison complexity T*(m,n) = O(m) for minimum spanning forests, yielding a uniform deterministic O(m) time MST algorithm on connected undirected multigraphs (O(m+n) for MSF) in the RAM and pointer-machine models via Pettie and Ramachandran's 2002 reduction.
assumptions: Unrefereed preprint whose main ideas are disclosed as generated by OpenAI Astra 6.2 and verified/simplified by the authors; no machine-checked formalization or implementation was provided or replayed here.

Linear running time follows indirectly via Pettie and Ramachandran's optimal-decision-tree reduction (using soft heaps and brute-force enumeration on small sub-instances), not from executing the preprint's schedule enumeration directly; no finite-size speedup over Kruskal, Prim or Boruvka is established.

The model assumes undirected multigraphs with pairwise-compared edge weights and deterministic tie-breaking; union-find's Omega(m alpha(m,n)) lower bound and fixed-tier placement/scheduling constraints remain unaffected.
